usage: Hello, who are you looking for?
examples: Hello? Is Mr. Kim Minsu there?
Hello, I cannot hear you well.
nuance: This word is used only on the phone, never face to face. It works both when you answer and when you start speaking to check the line.
mistakes: Do not use it when greeting someone in person

usage: Who is this? I cannot hear.
examples: Who is this? What is your name?
nuance: This polite phrase asks the identity of the caller without sounding rude. It is the standard way to find out who is speaking on the phone.
mistakes: Do not drop the honorific and say nuguya to strangers

usage: Is it okay to talk now?
Can you talk for a moment?
examples: Are you busy? Can you talk?
잠깐 통화 괜찮아요? 할 말이 있어요.
Can you talk briefly? I have something to say.
nuance: Koreans often ask this at the start of a call to show respect for the other person time. It checks whether the moment is convenient before continuing.
mistakes: Do not skip this when calling someone at work

usage: 다시 말해 주세요, 잘 안 들려요.
Please say it again, I cannot hear.
examples: 여보세요? 잘 안 들려요. 크게 말해 주세요.
Hello? I cannot hear well. Please speak louder.
미안해요, 잘 안 들려요. 다시 걸게요.
Sorry, I cannot hear. I will call again.
여기 신호가 약해서 잘 안 들려요.
The signal is weak here so I cannot hear.
nuance: This phrase politely tells the other person that the connection or volume is poor. It signals a problem without blaming anyone for the bad call.
mistakes: Do not say an deulyeo without the polite ending

examples: I am busy now so I will call back later.
I cannot hear. I will call back.
I will call back after the meeting.
nuance: Use this when you must end a call but plan to phone again yourself. The ending shows a friendly promise rather than a simple statement.
mistakes: Do not use this if the other person should call

examples: If the call fails I will text you.
I will text the time and place.
It is hard to talk now so I will text.
nuance: This is a common polite way to say you will follow up with a text message. The ending makes it sound like a warm promise to the listener.
mistakes: Do not confuse munja with jeonhwa meaning a call

usage: Please leave your name and message.
examples: 지금 안 계세요. 메모 남겨 주세요.
She is not here now. Please leave a message.
삐 소리 후에 메모 남겨 주세요.
Please leave a message after the beep.
I will pass it on. Please leave a message.
nuance: Use this when the person being called is unavailable and you want the caller to leave details. It is polite and common in offices and voicemail.
mistakes: Do not omit juseyo or it sounds like a command

usage: Wait, please do not hang up.
Please do not hang up the phone.
Please do not hang up yet.
examples: One moment, do not hang up. I will check.
Do not hang up, I will transfer you.
아직 할 말 있어요. 끊지 마세요.
I still have something to say. Do not hang up.
nuance: This phrase asks the other person to stay on the line while you do something. The polite ending keeps it firm but courteous during the call.
mistakes: Do not say kkeunchi ma which is too casual

examples: Please wait. He is not at his desk.
Yes, please wait. I will transfer you.
Please wait. I will find the note.
nuance: This is a gentle way to ask someone to hold on briefly during a call or in person. It buys you a short moment without sounding abrupt.
mistakes: Do not drop seyo when speaking to elders

usage: Please be sure to contact me.
Please contact me when you arrive.
examples: Please contact me when you are free.
Please contact me once you decide.
Please contact me anytime there is a problem.
nuance: Use this to politely ask someone to reach out to you by phone or message. It covers calls and texts and sounds warm and open.
mistakes: Do not confuse this with yeollak hasipsio which is formal

usage: Please put the person in charge on.
examples: Hello, please put Manager Park on.
If mom is there please put her on.
Sorry, please put the manager on.
nuance: On the phone this asks the person who answered to hand the call to someone else. The verb here means to switch the speaker, not to exchange goods.
mistakes: Do not think bakkwo only means exchange items

usage: Sorry, I dialed the wrong number.
Oh, I dialed the wrong number.
examples: I am sorry, I dialed the wrong number.
Oh, wrong number. I will hang up.
미안해요, 번호를 잘못 봐서 전화 잘못 걸었어요.
Sorry, I misread the number and dialed wrong.
nuance: Say this when you realize you have called the wrong person, usually with an apology. It politely closes the awkward moment before you hang up.
mistakes: Do not blame the listener for your own dialing error
